name: Annapurna Circuit Trek
summary: A circuit of the Annapurna massif, up the Marsyangdi valley to Manang, over the Thorong La at 5,416 m and down the Kali Gandaki past Muktinath and Jomsom. Roads now run far up both sides, so most walkers take jeeps at either end and the route is several days shorter than it once was.

name: Annapurna Circuit + Tilicho Lake
summary: The standard circuit with a three- to four-day detour from Manang up the Khangsar valley to Tilicho Lake at 4,919 m, rejoining the main trail before the Thorong La. The pass, not the lake, is still the highest point of the route.

name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
summary: The walk up the Modi Khola from Pokhara through Ghandruk and Chhomrong into the glacial basin below Annapurna I, finishing at the base camp lodges at 4,130 m. The upper gorge is avalanche-prone and is sometimes closed after heavy snow.

name: Annapurna Sanctuary Trek
summary: The same destination as the base camp trek — the amphitheatre of peaks enclosing the Annapurna basin — but usually sold as the longer version that takes in Ghorepani and Poon Hill before turning up the Modi Khola. The high point is the base camp at 4,130 m.

name: Mardi Himal Trek
summary: A short route on the ridge east of the Modi Khola, opened to lodges in 2012, climbing through rhododendron forest to High Camp at about 3,580 m and then along an exposed crest to the base camp below Mardi Himal at 4,500 m. Many walkers turn round at the viewpoint some 300 m lower.

name: Ghorepani–Poon Hill Trek
summary: A short loop through the middle hills from Nayapul, staying at Ghorepani for the pre-dawn climb to the Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210 m and usually returning by way of Ghandruk. The long stone staircase up to Ulleri is the hardest part of it.

name: Khopra Ridge Trek
summary: A quieter loop above the Ghorepani trails to the community lodge on Khopra Danda at 3,660 m, which faces Dhaulagiri across the Kali Gandaki. Itineraries sold as Khopra Ridge and Khayer Lake add a long day walk to the lake at about 4,660 m, which raises the high point of the route considerably.

name: Nar Phu Valley Trek
summary: A restricted-area route that branches north off the circuit at Koto into the Nar and Phu valleys, two Tibetan-speaking settlements, and leaves over the Kang La at 5,320 m to rejoin the main trail at Ngawal. A restricted-area permit, a licensed guide and a minimum party size are required.

name: Tilicho Lake Trek
summary: An out-and-back from the Marsyangdi valley through Manang and Khangsar to Tilicho Lake at 4,919 m, walked without crossing the Thorong La. The traverse into Tilicho Base Camp crosses a long slope of loose ground that is prone to rockfall.

name: Jomsom–Muktinath Trek
summary: The Kali Gandaki route between the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna massifs, walked up through Tatopani, Marpha and Jomsom to the temples at Muktinath, a site of pilgrimage for Hindus and Buddhists alike. It is often shortened by flying into Jomsom, and is walked in both directions.
